title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
- Establish a single, production-grade playbook for how Redwood teams detect, triage, mitigate, communicate, and learn from incidents that affect customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Provide templates and concrete runbooks so responders can act quickly and consistently.

Scope:
- This playbook applies to on-call SREs, service owners, product engineers, support, and customer-success who participate in incident management for Redwood Inference services.

Key goals (measurable):
- Time-to-acknowledge (P0): < 15 minutes on-call lead; P1: < 60 minutes.
- Mitigation goal (P0): initial mitigation (workaround/fallback) within 60 minutes; full recovery SLA timelines per SLA contract.
- Postmortem published within 72 hours (initial draft) and final within 14 days.

1) Roles & Responsibilities
- On-call SRE (primary responder): triage, runbook execution, coordinate mitigations, update status page.
- Service Owner: technical subject-matter expert for the affected service; owns post-incident action items and long-term fixes.
- Incident Commander (IC): assigned for P0/P1 incidents to drive the response and postmortem. Typically the on-call SRE for the service or designated senior engineer.
- Support / Customer Success: own customer comms and escalate external impact to sales/execs where appropriate.
- Engineering Manager / Product Manager: decision authority for customer-facing rollbacks or degradation policies.

2) Severity Definitions (standardized)
- P0 (Critical): Complete outage or severe degradation affecting >30% production requests or violating customer SLA. Must page on-call and senior leadership.
- P1 (High): Significant functional impact to a subset of customers or degraded latency/throughput causing business impact.
- P2 (Medium): Non-critical errors, isolated customer impacts, or performance regression that does not breach SLA.
- P3 (Low): Minor issues, docs/UX bugs, or non-urgent operational tasks.

3) Detection & Triage
- Alerts and Monitoring Sources:
  - Dashboards and alerts in Grafana/Prometheus (latency, error-rate, GPU OOMs, queue length).
  - Traces and logs (Jaeger, ELK).
  - Customer reports (support@redwood.ai, Zendesk ticket tagging: "incident").
  - PagerDuty for paging rules and escalation.
- Initial Triage Checklist (first 10 minutes):
  1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty.
  2. Determine scope: affected services, regions, customers, model variants.
  3. Check Grafana SLO dashboards and status page for known incidents.
  4. If P0/P1, assign an Incident Commander and set up a temporary incident channel (format: #incident-<short-id>) and a Zoom if needed.

4) Communication & Status Page
- Internal Communication:
  - Create incident Slack channel #incident-<short-id> (format: incident-YYYYMMDD-<service>). Post periodic updates (every 15-30 minutes for P0).
  - Update internal status in the incident channel: five-line summary, scope, impact, next steps, owners.
- External Communication / Status Page (customer-facing):
  - Use status.redwood.ai (Statuspage) templates. For P0 incidents update:
    - Affected services and regions.
    - Customer-visible symptoms (e.g., "text generation requests returning 500 / large latency spikes").
    - Mitigation actions and ETA for next update.
  - Customer comms templates included in Appendix A. Support owns sending targeted messages for impacted accounts.
- Example update cadence:
  - P0: initial post within 30 minutes, then every 30 minutes until mitigation, then hourly during recovery, final update with RCA and next steps.
  - P1: initial post within 60 minutes, then every 60-120 minutes.

5) Runbooks (how-to, one per common failure mode)
- Runbook structure (must be present at top of every runbook page):
  - Purpose and scope
  - Owner and runbook last-updated date
  - Page links: dashboards, logs, tracing, deploy history, recent rollouts
  - Immediate mitigation steps (step-by-step), diagnostic commands, and rollback/degrade options
  - Recovery verification steps and common postmortem signals to collect

- Example runbook: High 5xx rate for inference-service-api
  - Purpose: Mitigate sudden increase in 5xx responses from inference-service-api.
  - Owner: inference-service-team (oncall rotation).
  - Immediate steps:
    1. Check Grafana service error-rate and request volume (dashboard: /d/inference/errors).
    2. Identify specific 5xx pattern: 500 vs 502 vs 503 vs 504.
    3. If 503 with "capacity" errors, check Dedicated pool utilization (GPU pool dashboard). If saturated, scale burst pool or route to fallback model variant (routing policy: route->fallback-small-quantized).
    4. If 500 with model load errors, disable recent rollout: kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-service --namespace=prod (only after PM approval for risky rollbacks).
    5. If KV cache invalidation suspected, flush prefix cache for affected model: redis-cli -h cache-01 flushdb (followed by careful verification).
  - Verification: %5xx back to baseline for 15 minutes; end-to-end test prompt succeeds; lower tail latency restored.

6) Escalation Matrix and On-call Rotations
- Primary on-call (SRE): first responder via PagerDuty. If not acknowledged within 15 minutes for P0, page secondary on-call.
- Secondary on-call (service owner/SWE): stepped in after 15-30 minutes or on-demand for expertise.
- Tertiary escalation: engineering manager and platform lead for >60 minutes without mitigation or for decisions requiring wider approval.
- Rotation policies:
  - Typical cadence: 1-week rotations for platform SREs; 2-week rotations for service owners (adjust by team).
  - Shift handover: outgoing on-call must run a 15-minute handover with incoming on-call covering current alerts, ongoing incidents, and follow-up items. Record handover notes in the on-call calendar event.
  - Vacation and swap process: use the oncall-swaps tool (internal) and update PagerDuty schedule at least 48 hours before change.

7) Postmortems and Learning
- Postmortem timeline and expectations:
  1. Initial incident timeline and owner assigned within 24 hours.
  2. Draft postmortem published as a doc within 72 hours (initial RCA and action items).
  3. Final postmortem with mitigations, owners, and planned timeline for fixes within 14 days.
- Postmortem template (append in every postmortem doc):
  - Title, incident ID, severity, incident commander, affected services/regions, customer impact summary.
  - Timeline of events (UTC timestamps).
  - Root cause(s) and contributing factors.
  - Immediate mitigations and long-term fixes.
  - Action items (owner, due date, verification criterion).
  - Blameless analysis and follow-up game-day plan where appropriate.
- Review cadence: monthly "incident review" meeting across SRE + service owners for high-severity incidents to review action item progress and systemic trends.

8) Game Days and Drills
- Purpose: validate runbooks, escalation processes, and cross-team coordination.
- Frequency: quarterly company-wide game days; monthly smaller-scope drills for critical services.
- Types of drills:
  - Runbook validation: follow runbook steps in a controlled environment.
  - Chaos drills: simulate regional outages, GPU pool failures, and config drift.
  - Communication drills: test status page updates and customer comms.
- Game day checklist:
  1. Declare scope and objectives.
  2. Notify stakeholders and schedule time window.
  3. Assign observers and documenters.
  4. Run drill, capture timeline, and collect metrics.
  5. Post-drill postmortem and remediation actions.

9) Status Page & Customer Communications Templates (Appendix A)
- Status post structure:
  - Summary (1 sentence)
  - Impact (who/how many customers/regions)
  - Root cause (high level)
  - Mitigation steps taken and next steps
  - ETA for next update
  - Contact for support (support@redwood.ai)

- Example customer-facing update (P0 initial):
  "We are investigating increased 500 responses for the Redwood Hosted API in us-west-2. Customers may experience failed requests and elevated latency. Our on-call engineers are actively triaging the issue. Next update in 30 minutes. For support, contact support@redwood.ai."

- Example targeted email for affected customers (use Support to populate customer list):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident impacting inference requests in us-west-2
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  We are currently investigating an incident affecting inference request success rates in us-west-2. Our teams are working on mitigation. We will share updates via status.redwood.ai and directly through this thread. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

10) Telemetry and Evidence Collection
- Required artifacts to capture for every incident:
  - Alert IDs, graphs (png export), traces (Jaeger links), affected request IDs, deploy history, and relevant logs (time-windowed).
  - Postmortem must include links to dashboards and raw evidence attachments in the doc.

11) Metrics & SLOs to Monitor (examples)
- API Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for hosted API (per SLA).
- Median inference latency (p50) target: < 50ms for small models; tail p95/p99 monitored per model class.
- 5xx rate alert thresholds: >0.5% baseline -> paging threshold; >1% sustained for 5 minutes -> P1/P0 alert escalation.

12) Templates and Checklists (Appendix B)
- Incident start checklist (first 15 minutes)
  - Acknowledge and document initial symptoms.
  - Create incident channel, assign IC, notify support and product.
  - Post initial status page update if customers impacted.
- Incident end checklist
  - Confirm recovery and run verification tests.
  - Close all related PagerDuty alerts.
  - Publish postmortem draft and assign action items.

Appendix A: Customer comms and status page templates (copyable)
- See "Status post structure" and sample messages above.

Appendix B: Runbook examples and useful commands
- kubectl commands (must be executed only by authorized responders):
  - kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-service
  - kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-service -n prod
  - curl -sS https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/pages/updates (internal tooling)

Appendix C: Postmortem checklist (must be included with every postmortem doc)
- Add timeline and raw evidence links.
- Assign owners and due dates for each action item.
- Link to runbook updates required and schedule a small game-day to validate fixes.

Appendix D: Contact and escalation list
- PagerDuty schedule: https://pagerduty.com/orgs/redwood/schedules
- Slack channels:
  - #incident-ops (ops coordination)
  - #status-updates (exec summaries)
  - #oncall-handoffs (handovers and swaps)
- On-call coordinator: oncall-coordinator@redwood.ai
